references.text: The description of the veil (parokhet) that was to separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy, where the ark of the testimony was to be placed.
Instructions concerning the mercy seat (kapporet) that was to be placed above the testimony, and where God promised to meet Moses.
The testimony (edut) that was to be placed in the ark, referred to in our text as the 'ark of the covenant'.
God promises to meet the children of Israel at the entrance of the tent sanctuary, where He will speak with them.
Fulfillment of the command to place the golden altar for incense before the ark of the testimony.
The Lord reveals Himself in the cloud above the mercy seat, which is mentioned in connection with the altar of incense.
Moses heard God's voice speaking to him from the mercy seat between the cherubim, just as God promised to meet him there.
The letter to the Hebrews describes the furnishings in the Most Holy Place, including the golden altar for incense and the ark of the covenant with its mercy seat.
Both verses define the holy space as God's meeting place with the people at the ark of the testimony.
Understanding the placement of the altar of incense in the Holy Place only through understanding the dividing veil (parokhet) toward the Most Holy Place.
Direct theological parallel: Incense (or the altar) is placed by the testimony to enable God's meeting with the people.
